newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela to sell Banco de Venezuela in Q4 1996.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela to sell Banco de Venezuela in Q4 1996.

text.p: Venezuela's state Desposits Guarantee Fund (FOGADE) aims to sell state bank Banco de Venezuela, the auction of which was canecelled this week, in the fourth quarter of this year, FOGADE President Esther de Margulis said.
Margulis, who on Wednesday announced the surprise cancellation of Friday's planned auction, told a news conference the government decided to reconvene the auction.
"In this way the government shows its unshakable will to continue with the privatization process," she said.
The $275 million base price set for Friday's auction could be changed, "according to the financial information closer to the date," Margulis said.
The conditions of the new auction are still under study, she added.
Margulis announced on Wednesday that the planned auction of Banco de Venezuela had been called off indefinitely because of confusions about the auction.
Spain's Banco Santander, Peru's Banco de Credito, Colombia's Banco Bogota and Germany's Dresdner Bank AG had shown interest in the bank, but only the first two placed a deposit needed to make a bid.

Margulis said the new auction process could mean some of these potential bidders would drop out, while others may join in. The decision to call off Friday's auction cast a large shadow over Venezuela's struggling privatization program.
Margulis said the fourth quarter sale of Banco de Venezuela would be joined by Banco de Consolidado. Banco Latino and Banco Republica will be sold in early 1997, she added.
FOGADE took over the banks during the 1994-95 financial sector crisis which claimed over half the commercial banking sector and cost the state over $10 billion.
Banco de Venezuela, the country's oldest bank, was the third largest commercial bank at the end of July with 418 billion bolivars worth ($880 million) in deposits.
